headline: Public pages no longer answer 403 to search-engine crawlers
summary: If anything you host is meant to be found — a public stash portal, a share link, a landing page — this is worth taking. The bot filter refused any request that omitted an Accept-Language header, and every major search-engine crawler omits it. A browser was served normally, so the refusal was invisible unless you looked at what a crawler received.

items.title: Stop refusing requests that omit Accept-Language
items.body:
The bot filter treated a missing Accept-Language header as grounds for a 403. Google documents that Googlebot sends requests without setting it, and bingbot behaves the same, so every public page answered 403 to a crawler while a browser sailed through. Uptime monitors, link previewers and feed readers were refused the same way. The header's absence is now an advisory signal, matching how the same filter already treats a missing Sec-Fetch-Mode.

What still refuses a request has not been loosened. Automation libraries are refused by their User-Agent, and a request carrying no User-Agent at all is refused too — a crawler identifies itself in that header, so the empty case stays blocked without taking the crawlers with it. A raw header-less GET to a page route is still turned away.

items.title: Vendored blamejs moves to 0.18.43
items.body: Carries the framework side of the fix above. The nested certificate toolkit moves to 0.5.17, where a failed integrity check now destroys the plaintext it had recovered instead of returning it, and an authenticated-encryption container validates the attributes it is asked to authenticate. Neither path is reachable from this server, which uses the toolkit for its certificate authorities rather than for message containers.
